projects.create.rules: Feature budget authoring (schema3) is feature-only: omitted existing/imported values preserve configuration, new feature defaultsOff. Only actual human authority may raise/remove an existing cap. Draft/import cap changes apply only with exact human approval; staging is not adoption. Raising/Off never clears a budget Continue latch or other holds. Issues/tasks/jobs have no independent cap.

projects.membership.rules: Replace membership atomically; authorize every added/removed repository and preserve shared registrations.

projects.archive.rules: Archive immediately fences active work. Deletion tombstones app records; never removes source Git resources. Concrete destructive confirmation where required.

projects.restore.rules: Archive immediately fences active work. Deletion tombstones app records; never removes source Git resources. Concrete destructive confirmation where required.

projects.delete.rules: Archive immediately fences active work. Deletion tombstones app records; never removes source Git resources. Concrete destructive confirmation where required.

features.get.rules: Read one feature at its work revision. Schema revision 2: the record carries the feature's current execution-readiness assessment (AGENT-12, AGENT-18-20): the reviewed plan revision and digest, freshness against the active approved plan (stale scope units by requirement ID; the absent key is feature-wide), whether it is ready (current with no open blocking finding) and every finding with its requirement links, disposition, affected work, attempts, closure condition, decision with confidence and evidence, investigation objective/limits, question/recommendation and closure evidence. Readiness is reported separately from plan approval. Every work record at revision 2 also carries the revision of the queue it is ranked in (queueRevision: the project queue for features and standalone issues, its feature queue for a card) and of its project workflow (workflowRevision), the expected revisions of prioritization and workflow moves. A feature record at revision 2 also carries its active plan's acceptance tests (acceptanceTests), so a client revising the plan keeps them.

features.create.rules: Host fixes kind=Feature. A feature has no task parent; project tasks may have an optional feature relationship. Schema revision 3: optional labels replace the exact bounded set (empty clears; omitted preserves updates). Task/issue patches and task plan entries accept taskType or clearTaskType:true, never both. Features carry labels but no card type. Invalid duplicate/whitespace-only labels and conflicting clear/set are refused atomically. Draft/import cap changes apply only with exact human approval; staging is not adoption. Raising/Off never clears a budget Continue latch or other holds. Issues/tasks/jobs have no independent cap.

features.edit.rules: Metadata edits do not replace the effective approved plan. Changes to structured implementation scope, repositories/goals or acceptance of an approved feature must use the pending-plan flow; refuse bypass through generic edits. Current title/description prose does not grant new implementation authority. Schema revision 2: readiness records an assessment of the current active or pending plan (bound to its revision and digest; findings are validated against its requirements and the feature's work, a new blocking finding at an unchanged plan needs new evidence, settled findings are not reopened without it) or closes one finding with its closure note and evidence. Readiness is derived, never caller-asserted; plan approval never closes findings. Schema revision 2: acceptanceEvidence records the state and evidence of the active plan's acceptance criteria and acceptance tests (by ID, at their approved text; evidence IDs are recorded history links of the project). A feature in a Done status is Verified only when every such criterion is met with evidence, otherwise Manual; only Verified completion satisfies its dependents. Schema revision 3: optional labels replace the exact bounded set (empty clears; omitted preserves updates). Task/issue patches and task plan entries accept taskType or clearTaskType:true, never both. Features carry labels but no card type. Invalid duplicate/whitespace-only labels and conflicting clear/set are refused atomically. issues.create.rules: Create one project-owned task identity. Optional featureId uses the same membership transition/coordination rules as tasks.set_feature; no feature is required. A linked issue is a delivery obligation without revised-plan approval. Preserve issue/task identity and execution controls. Schema revision 3 may author Story/Task/Bug taskType and bounded unique labels; metadata has no effect on execution kind, authority or blockers.

issues.edit.rules: Standalone issue priority uses the same task priority use case and project root queue; preserve stable work identity and all execution controls. Schema revision 3: optional labels replace the exact bounded set (empty clears; omitted preserves updates). Task/issue patches and task plan entries accept taskType or clearTaskType:true, never both. Features carry labels but no card type. Invalid duplicate/whitespace-only labels and conflicting clear/set are refused atomically.

tasks.list.rules: Return tasks in declared queue order with priority/manual rank and bounded blocked-by/dependent IDs, actual coverage and detail cursor; exact eligibility remains a current host check.

tasks.create.rules: Project is required; parentId is an optional feature relationship, not an assignment parent. Validate any feature belongs to the same project. Without a feature, create a standalone project task shown as an issue; do not manufacture a feature or duplicate its identity. Standalone tasks use issue execution/accounting/delivery policy. Task operations accept Task/Issue representations of the same project-task model. Schema revision 3 may author Story/Task/Bug taskType and bounded unique labels; metadata has no effect on execution kind, authority or blockers.

tasks.edit.rules: Task/issue priority edits use current work revision and the same priority use case as tasks.prioritize; update the owning queue revision and history atomically. A priority edit alone does not stop active work, clear blockers or invalidate the approved feature plan. Schema revision 3: optional labels replace the exact bounded set (empty clears; omitted preserves updates). Task/issue patches and task plan entries accept taskType or clearTaskType:true, never both. Features carry labels but no card type. Invalid duplicate/whitespace-only labels and conflicting clear/set are refused atomically.

features.prioritize.rules: IDs unique and scoped; preserve omitted work relative order. Feature and issue priorities share one project queue. Schema revision 2: placement instead moves one item immediately before or after an anchor of the same queue and priority bucket (one bounded request for any bucket size); exactly one of the ordered IDs and placement.

issues.prioritize.rules: IDs unique and scoped; preserve omitted work relative order. Feature and issue priorities share one project queue. Schema revision 2: placement instead moves one item immediately before or after an anchor of the same queue and priority bucket (one bounded request for any bucket size); exactly one of the ordered IDs and placement.

features.edit_plan.rules: Save or edit the feature-owned pending plan only. Preserve the active plan, its approval and currently effective scope/acceptance while the revision awaits approval or is rejected. Editing a pending proposal invalidates only that proposal approval. No active plan exists before initial approval. Approval through authenticated human decision atomically promotes the exact reviewed pending plan and updates effective fields, history and wakeups; never start/resume from edit alone. Plan revision/digest fields are internal conflict and approval-binding tokens, not user-facing plan versions. Missing active requirements in the replacement require explicit Dropped decisions; do not rewrite current task acceptance during drafting. Schema3 optional budget is a proposed feature cap change beside the pending PlanDraft, not effective configuration. Omission preserves the effective cap. Bind it in the exact pending digest/approval, expose it on PendingFeaturePlan for reopened editors, and adopt only on actual human approval. Direct effective cap lifts/removal remain human-only. Editing alone never clears budget/other holds. Omission preserves an existing pending budget proposal for legacy clients. Schema3 clearBudgetProposal:true explicitly withdraws only the pending cap proposal, never the effective budget; it is exclusive with budget (including explicit Off). Null or false clearBudgetProposal is invalid.

features.dependencies.rules: Validate scoped references and reject cycles atomically.

features.request_plan_approval.rules: Bind the exact pending plan revision/digest, not the active plan. Requesting approval does not clear the original approval, block otherwise eligible work, or execute pending scope. A changed pending draft makes the old proposal stale. Approval atomically promotes it; rejection leaves active plan and controls unchanged.

issues.publish.rules: Reconcile saved remote identity after an uncertain create; no duplicate publish.

tasks.assign.rules: Set or explicit clear, exactly one; assignment belongs to the same root and authority generation. Membership changes use tasks.set_feature; preserve original assignment lineage while rebinding current supervisor/admission at a safe boundary.

tasks.dependency_links.rules: Replace exactly the incoming blocking links of taskId: predecessor blocks successor and every supplied successor must equal taskId. Empty edges explicitly removes those links only. Validate current project membership/access for both endpoints; permit same-project cross-feature and standalone-task links without changing feature membership. Reject self-links, duplicates and project-wide cycles atomically under the write owner; bounded reachability failure cannot authorize an unchecked link. Recheck target expectedRevision and current graph, commit link set, task/queue revisions, reciprocal derived reads, history/receipt/wakeup together. Unsatisfied prerequisites block claim and new dependent dispatch even at higher priority. Required completion is verified acceptance/integration under the prerequisite existing policy, not a manual Done label or process exit. A new blocker on active work fences affected new dispatch and requests safe interruption/reconciliation; it does not erase completed effects. Removing/satisfying it triggers eligibility reevaluation without clearing pauses/approvals/budgets. Completed work is not reopened by link editing; require explicit reopen before changing its execution prerequisites. No dependency itself moves code between branches or grants merge authority.

tasks.sync_plan.rules: Atomic upsert by client key with explicit desired task relationships; reject conflicting edits and cycles, preserve evidence. Missing tasks are not silently deleted. Optional atomic project plan preserves caller refs, feature requirements and task inheritance; validate all feature/task revisions and all references/cycles before any write. Missing active requirements need explicit drop decisions; absent tasks are never silently deleted. Larger source plans use an authorized immutable artifact validated against the fixed AtomicWorkPlan schema, retaining atomicity beyond the wire-frame limit; inline/staged project plan are mutually exclusive. Routine decomposition within the active approved plan remains allowed. A pending plan does not authorize changing live task scope or acceptance beyond that plan; proposed dependent work waits for plan approval. Atomic project-plan entry points must preserve the same active/pending distinction and cannot invalidate the active approval merely by saving a draft. Optional task priorities preserve existing values when omitted; new tasks use the documented default. Routine priority/dependency coordination uses the same shared validation and does not invalidate the active plan approval. Project-wide cycle validation includes links to tasks outside the feature. Schema revision 3: optional labels replace the exact bounded set (empty clears; omitted preserves updates). Task/issue patches and task plan entries accept taskType or clearTaskType:true, never both. Features carry labels but no card type. Invalid duplicate/whitespace-only labels and conflicting clear/set are refused atomically. Draft/import cap changes apply only with exact human approval; staging is not adoption. Raising/Off never clears a budget Continue latch or other holds. Issues/tasks/jobs have no independent cap.

workflows.reassign_and_remove.rules: Move all affected work and remove status atomically; destination differs and retains valid category.

next_work.claim_project_queue.rules: Actor/owner derived from host. Atomically select current eligible unclaimed feature/issue. Automatic feature claims require implementation approval; never clear holds. Schema revision 3 returns allocation-specific work kind/revision, project/root, optional durable owner session and queue revision after the atomic claim transition. Existing ClaimRecord embedded in WorkRecord stays unchanged. No eligible candidate returns a typed DomainFault with targetKind no_eligible_work and evidence, never a fabricated claim ID. Receipt replay preserves its original claim and never consumes a second allocation turn. Revision 3 supports repository/card-type/label filters and explicit another selection, preserves existing caller claims by default, and returns Claimed, Recovered or NoEligible outcomes with bounded current work/recovery evidence. Host actor/session and ingress identity replace caller-authored authority markers. Optional idempotencyKey is a project/caller-scoped allocation identity in addition to the runtime requestKey, preserving retries without another allocation. Recovery precedes new work where the retained source requires it; preserve previous-holder, Git/PR links, latest handoff, last activity and unmet acceptance truthfully. Legacy revision-1 successful results project to exact ClaimRecord; NoEligible remains a typed fault at revision1.

runs.redirect.rules: Persist redirect identity/stages; incorporated only at coordinator safe boundary. Does not clear pause or bypass Continue.

runs.stop.rules: Cancel/quiesce owned work under root fencing; uncertain effects remain held until reconciled. No manual child control.

agents.delegate.rules: Owner/parent and root scope from invocation. A root issue and scoped brief suffice; taskIds may be empty. Optional task references must belong to the same project and authorized root scope; no feature or feature card is required for issue delegation. Independent configurable per-root cap defaults to10; no global cap. Assignment parentage is independent of optional task-to-feature association; role cannot expand access or waive a blocker.

agents.messages.rules: Durable send/ack lineage. Sender/root/parent/authority are host-derived; cross-root or revoked recipients rejected. Inbox reads are separate and cannot acknowledge delivery.

agents.post.rules: Additive retained-source post contract. The gateway-selected command and current principal bind the sender; optional session/project must match current authority. Route, reply resolution, blocking and idempotency are validated by the retained message service.

agents.receive.rules: Additive retained-source receive. The current principal selects its own session or the project's human inbox; cursor is an opaque inbox position, default zero, and unacknowledged deliveries replay. At most 55 seconds of polling in separate short snapshots precedes one transactional delivery and command receipt; cancellation leaves no receipt.

agents.ack.rules: Additive retained-source acknowledgment. Exactly one of message ids or an opaque next_cursor from the addressed inbox; resolution requires named messages. Current principal binds the recipient, and a repeated acknowledgment is a no-op. First/last blocking-question resolution atomically updates affected work versions.

agents.history.rules: Human project-scoped retained message history newest first. Filters and before cursor are checked against current item/feature ownership; the next_before cursor continues the recorded order without a write. Agent sessions read their addressed inbox instead of the full project history.

agents.events.rules: Human project message event cursor. An absent cursor starts at the current head; an explicit cursor resumes committed later events in order, and an ahead cursor refuses after restore. Streaming callers repeat the query without holding a connection.

sessions.briefing.rules: Schema revision 2: item adds that visible work item of the session's scope to the briefing; paths (distinct) scope it; budgetTokens caps the summed source estimates (4 bytes per token, rounded up) at a prefix of the briefing order.

sessions.start.rules: Creates conversation only; cannot Start/Continue work or duplicate an existing root coordinator.

sessions.end.rules: Closes selected conversation at a safe boundary; active root work requires ordinary root stop/pause controls, never silent termination.

ui.current_screen.rules: Host supplies bounded current selection/help context. No caller-written screen state or hidden pane authority.

history.work_lineage.rules: Schema revision 2: every page carries a continuation checkpoint, including at the current tail; records carry structured attribution.

history.git_links.rules: Schema revision 2: every page carries a continuation checkpoint, including at the current tail; records carry structured attribution.

history.evidence_links.rules: Schema revision 2: every page carries a continuation checkpoint, including at the current tail; records carry structured attribution.

history.tool_usage.rules: Exactly one of rootId, projectId (revision 2) and workspace: true (revision 2). Schema revision 2: tool invocations (one per durable initial tool response of any session in the scope) are interleaved with inference usage in committed-sequence order, each list carries its committed sequences, and every page carries a continuation checkpoint.

indexing.index.rules: Capture exact source revision, stage and publish under a current fence; partial/failed extraction never becomes complete.

indexing.reindex.rules: Capture exact source revision, stage and publish under a current fence; partial/failed extraction never becomes complete.

indexing.retire_view.rules: Retire eligibility before GC; live pins/references preserve bytes until safe collection.

indexing.status.rules: Exactly one of repositoryId and overlayId (revision 2). Schema revision 2: freshness (the indexed and observed HEAD commits, configuration currency and stale reasons), per-language structural/text coverage with grammar identity, semantic pack state, and every overlay of the repository with its lifecycle state (Queued, Indexing, Ready, Failed, Stale, Expired, Unavailable) and snapshot provenance. With overlayId (an overlay of a repository the caller may see), the result is that repository's status whose overlays member holds exactly that overlay. An overlay requested by ref has no worktreeId.

indexing.runs.rules: Schema revision 2: states keeps only runs in one of the listed run states (Queued, Running, Succeeded, Failed, Cancelled; a record reports Queued as IntentRecorded or RetryPending, Running as Dispatching, Succeeded as ObservedComplete and Cancelled as CancelledBeforeDispatch) and kinds only runs of one of the listed kinds (Index, Reindex, Overlay); both are optional and combine, and a continuation cursor is bound to them.
