schemas.connections.rules: Revision5 publishes source access/profile/freshness and typed metadata details; scope and current authority precede pagination. No source row values are retained.

schemas.objects.rules: Revision5 publishes source access/profile/freshness and typed metadata details; scope and current authority precede pagination. No source row values are retained.

schemas.relationships.rules: Revision5 publishes source access/profile/freshness and typed metadata details; scope and current authority precede pagination. No source row values are retained.

schemas.index.rules: Metadata-only credential/profile; never persist source row values. Qualify actual read-only metadata enforcement for engine. Revision5 testOnly validates the actual metadata connection/profile without publishing a schema view; normal indexing atomically publishes an immutable scoped metadata snapshot, preserving last-good data on failure.

schemas.refresh.rules: Metadata-only credential/profile; never persist source row values. Qualify actual read-only metadata enforcement for engine. Revision5 testOnly uses the same bounded native metadata probe. Native sync-all independently admits every eligible source through this operation and reports each outcome.

schemas.configure.rules: Create or compare-and-edit; credential references are host-issued. HelixDB source reading is excluded; reject unsupported engines. App persistence uses SQLite/FTS5/sqlite-vec. Revision5 Save configures enablement, explicit project access, exposure and qualified auth/TLS; Remove retires the definition and indexed metadata without altering the source database. Only native Human configuration may change connection/global/project write policy; no policy grants implicit target execution.

database.read.rules: Parse/check effective read-only operation through qualified adapter; no arbitrary SQL function side effects, sensitive-column policy before materialization. Results not structural graph persistence.

database.execute_write.rules: Connection writes enabled and current scoped write authority. Exact target/digest approval where required. Transaction/unknown commit reconciled before retry; not authorized by a read entitlement.

database.direct_schema_change.rules: Connection writes enabled and current scoped write authority. Exact target/digest approval where required. Transaction/unknown commit reconciled before retry; not authorized by a read entitlement.

database.apply_migration.rules: Versioned immutable migration; exact target authority independent of artifact read. Unknown application status reconciled through migration evidence.

knowledge.search.rules: Scoped lexical search, newest first: a project scope reads that project and general (workspace) Knowledge, a workspace scope only general Knowledge; scope applies before any candidate is materialized. Every word of text must appear (Unicode case-folded) in the claim or its subject entity. Lifecycle Active by default (revision 1: Active only). Cursors bind the query and the revisions of every scope read. Schema revision 2: lifecycle states, entry kinds, source and stale filters; claims carry provenance, lifecycle, verification and lesson state.

knowledge.read.rules: One visible claim with its subject/object entities, evidence, open conflicts (active claims of the same subject and predicate with another value) and supersession chain; revision reads a recorded past revision. Schema revision 2: relations, revision history and the scope revision.

knowledge.record.rules: Atomic entity/claim/evidence validation; client IDs resolve within batch; claims need object or value, not neither. Preserve provenance and contradictory claims.

knowledge.revise.rules: A new revision of an active claim at its exact revision.

knowledge.relate.rules: Typed attributed relation between visible entities or claims of the scope. Lessons: same_as merges the subject into the object as recurrence, contradicts keeps both with an open conflict, unmerge reverses a same_as merge.

knowledge.tag.rules: Replace each selected claim's tag set (Unicode case-folded, sorted, unique) at its exact revision.

knowledge.verify.rules: Append attributed state/evidence; never erase contradiction or overwrite a newer authored revision. Schema revision 2: the source revision verified against; a later observed source revision marks the claim stale until verified again.

knowledge.retract.rules: Mark an active claim wrong at its exact revision; it stays readable as Retracted.

knowledge.challenge.rules: Append attributed state/evidence; never erase contradiction or overwrite a newer authored revision. Schema revision 2: resolve an open challenge (Uphold or Retire) or, with outcome Retire and no challenge, retire the rule; a resolution is the user's and nothing waits on a challenge.

knowledge.scope.rules: Authorize source and destination before atomic move; visibility changes invalidate affected retrieval scopes.

knowledge.diagnostics.rules: Counts, retrieval mode and recent write outcomes of a visible scope; the reply stamp carries the scope revision. Diagnostic codes: component knowledge.retrieval code LexicalOnly while no embedding route exists (vector search is never claimed); component knowledge.counts per lifecycle and lesson state; component knowledge.writes for recent writes. Schema revision 2: sourceId previews a delete by source and importSource with importSchema previews a user data import, each as a component knowledge.preview diagnostic whose id is the exact preview digest, plus one knowledge.import diagnostic per candidate with its outcome. Schema revision 3: sourceLabel accepts the full recorded source label, as an alternative to legacy sourceId; never supply both.

knowledge.delete_by_source.rules: Exact preview match; tombstone selected source contributions, preserve independent surviving evidence and journal count. Any size of source is deleted whole: past one batch it continues as a durable job (each batch its own transaction, resumed at boot), the source of the scope is read-only until it finishes, and knowledge.write_status of the summary id reports Dispatching, then ObservedComplete with every ID. Schema revision 3: sourceLabel accepts the full recorded source label, as an alternative to legacy sourceId; never supply both.

knowledge.delete_selected.rules: The user or host only. Exact revisions; tombstone the selected claims (provenance kept, content purged) and evidence no surviving claim uses; journal counts.

knowledge.write_status.rules: The durable receipt of a committed Knowledge write. Schema revision 2: entityCount and claimCount are the totals the write changed; a receipt names at most 128 entity IDs, claim IDs and diagnostics, and nextCursor (when any list has more) continues through write_status with cursor, so every ID and note of a bulk write is readable and none is dropped.

knowledge.subgraph.rules: Apply scope before expansion and bound visited/output work; stable cursor pins query/scope/view. Empty explicit IDs cannot turn into unrestricted scan.

knowledge.entity_bundle.rules: Apply scope before expansion and bound visited/output work; stable cursor pins query/scope/view. Empty explicit IDs cannot turn into unrestricted scan.

knowledge.entity_graph.rules: Apply scope before expansion and bound visited/output work; stable cursor pins query/scope/view. Empty explicit IDs cannot turn into unrestricted scan.

knowledge.claim_bundle.rules: Apply scope before expansion and bound visited/output work; stable cursor pins query/scope/view. Empty explicit IDs cannot turn into unrestricted scan.

knowledge.expand_frontier.rules: Apply scope before expansion and bound visited/output work; stable cursor pins query/scope/view. Empty explicit IDs cannot turn into unrestricted scan.

knowledge.query.rules: Apply scope before expansion and bound visited/output work; stable cursor pins query/scope/view. Empty explicit IDs cannot turn into unrestricted scan.

knowledge.render_summary.rules: Deterministic bounded rendering of observed claims; model synthesis is separate attributed inference, not hidden query side effect.

knowledge.import_user_data.rules: User-authored data import only; legacy CodeGraph Knowledge migration excluded. Preview exact immutable source; retain evidence and idempotent identity map.

knowledge.promote.rules: Authorize both scopes and preserve original provenance/version. Promotion grants no instruction or execution authority. Schema revision 2: action Effective (default; the user makes a lesson an effective rule early), Propose, Reject (the user, with reason) or Address (a lesson addressed in code, instructions, a skill, documentation or a test). No rule waits for approval.

knowledge.tagged_lessons.rules: Lessons carrying every tag, newest first: a project scope reads its own and general lessons. Schema revision 2: rule states, activity and views (recently learned, recurring, unaddressed, undelivered).

dreaming.run.rules: Current scheduler/user authority; saved checkpoint exact inputs, no inference while paused/blocked. Proposed changes stay attributed.

dreaming.revert.rules: Revert only attributable unchanged effects; intervening user edits require conflict handling, never destructive restore.

dreaming.review.rules: Host mints decision from explicit human interaction; an agent may propose or read, never self-approve.

documents.import.rules: Replacement names target/revision and creates immutable retained version; native PDF/MD/text/DOCX only. Exact source pin, extraction diagnostics and bounded outputs.

documents.index.rules: Native extraction first; scan vision/embedding uses router and ordinary usage/feature budget attribution. Failed/canceled old version cannot publish current results.

documents.retry.rules: Native extraction first; scan vision/embedding uses router and ordinary usage/feature budget attribution. Failed/canceled old version cannot publish current results.

conventions.retire.rules: Retires the exact convention or cancels its owned pending operation. Attachment content is never a RAG target.

conventions.index.rules: Indexes convention page bodies only; attachment targets are unsupported. Exact captured content and current source/authority fences govern publication.

conventions.delete.rules: Delete resource requires exact registered resource ID. Authored content/retained references never removed by index retirement.

conventions.delete_resource.rules: Delete resource requires exact registered resource ID. Authored content/retained references never removed by index retirement.

conventions.import.rules: Explicit user-authored import only; excluded legacy conventions migration remains excluded.

skills.draft.rules: Stage local override or new candidate; shared original untouched and no activation by writing.

skills.propose.rules: Exact version/content approval for agent-authored executable/instruction changes; adoption only at safe boundary.

skills.rollback.rules: New attributed revision restores approved content; do not rewrite history or activate beyond current authority.

roles.draft.rules: Stage local override or new candidate; shared original untouched and no activation by writing.

roles.propose.rules: Exact version/content approval for agent-authored executable/instruction changes; adoption only at safe boundary.

roles.rollback.rules: New attributed revision restores approved content; do not rewrite history or activate beyond current authority.

skills.resources.rules: Revision 3 returns each resource of the skill revision with its skill-relative path and executable flag beside its artifact; revision 1 returns the same artifacts, in the same order, without them.

approvals.inspect.rules: Revision 3 inspect returns exact typed reviewedSource for source-owned settings/feature plans, including legal content larger than the DynamicJson metadata limit. List rows omit reviewedSource. reviewedContent remains bounded metadata; never silently truncate or substitute a digest for human-readable reviewed source.

approvals.propose.rules: Proposal operation/target/schema must match registered approvable capability; no generic approval-token factory. Schema 3 payload selects immutable settings entries, an existing feature-plan proposal, exact finding assessment, or a saved registered operation. SavedOperation.input is the closed argument body without envelope/kind/caller-authority fields; its positive schema revision must fit u16 and be registered. Actual admission derives normalized request/effect/targets; owner preflight remains mandatory. Snapshot and provenance bind exact content, target revision and digest. Disabled, read-only and hard-blocked capabilities are never waived.

approvals.record_human_decision.rules: Authenticated host human-event context only, never callable with self-claimed human=true. Binds exact proposal/target/digest; does not Continue paused root. For feature-plan proposals, recheck the exact pending draft/content and human authority, then atomically replace active plan/approval/effective scope and publish the adoption event. Rejection or stale approval leaves the active plan unchanged. Neither outcome clears manual holds. Human witness and saved-operation resume grant are private host context, never wire fields. Original actor/context remain original; a narrow reviewed-operation proof records the deciding human separately. Finding risk acceptance binds the specific finding, assessment/scope revision and rationale; generic acknowledgment cannot close findings.

notifications.list.rules: Per-recipient durable notification projection. Completion category is Completion; completion cards use newest-first stable (createdAtMs,id) ordering and sourceId deduplication. Read state and acknowledgment are independent; filters do not mutate either.

notifications.read.rules: Pure detail query. Opening/reading a notification never marks read, acknowledges, dismisses or resolves its linked decision.

notifications.acknowledge.rules: Explicit durable individual completion-card dismissal, retained in history across navigation/restart. Acknowledgment cannot approve/resolve a linked human decision or resume paused work.

git.worktree.rules: Create/attach only app-owned registered resources at exact base; no arbitrary path. Parent work determines feature/issue branch target.

reviews.request.rules: Use supported repository-configured GitHub source identity/adapter and exact barrier heads/policy. Explicit completed evidence including zero findings is required. Failure/unavailability or finite deadline expiry admits one independent verified-read in-app fallback per repository/PR/head/policy/cycle. Fallback does not waive required checks or branch protection and does not itself spend a fix cycle. Preserve late external actionable findings. No role grants approval/mutation rights.

reviews.adjudicate.rules: Resolve through configured independent review policy; author cannot self-waive required review without explicit policy authority.

reviews.readiness.rules: Require current exact-head completed source evidence with complete findings coverage, explicit zero-findings outcome when empty and all actionable findings resolved. Preserve late external findings and policy/head invalidation; absence of comments or unrelated passing checks never qualifies. Fallback replaces only the DevWorks review source.

github.account.rules: One GitHub.com account; credentials handled by native host sign-in flow, never ordinary config payload/logs.

github.poll_status.rules: Include persisted issue intake/admission timing and pending/failed resolution observations; scope unrouted incoming reports by repository access. No agent is required to inspect a waiting queue.

github.issue_sync.rules: Conditional paginated inbound capture plus verified-resolution outbox reconciliation, not a mirror of local tracking fields. Reuse repository/issue identity. Queue routing/triage globally using app-only github.issueTriageIntervalSeconds (positive seconds, default1800), one admission per interval with persisted timing and no catch-up burst. Import/polling alone launches no agent outside this gate. Triage routes shared-repository reports, verifies bugs and starts verifiable bugs when eligible; notify for feature requests/unverifiable bugs/new scope. Remote closure preserves started verified fixes and approved/planned feature work. Automatic publication requires verified accepted completion and integration; resolve uncertain summary/close effects before retry. Existing human pauses cannot be cleared by import/reopen. Route distinct multi-project work through related project-owned obligations on the same remote source; resolution publication waits for its current included obligation set and uses one durable publisher receipt, not a repository-wide project owner.

resources.list.rules: Schema revision 2: records carry scope, physical, labels, occupancy, purpose, priority, queue position, lifecycle times, end reason, unreachable ownership and the owning project, work, assignment and session.

resources.acquire.rules: Host derives owner and canonical physical identity; current assignment/root grant. Wait instead of oversubscribe; no release while physical outcome uncertain. Schema revision 2: purpose (at most 500 characters) and priority (default Medium) are recorded on the lease; waiters are served by priority, first come first served within one; capacity (default 1) and labels (at most 20 of at most 64 characters) apply when the call creates a project resource and must equal an existing one.

resources.renew.rules: Schema revision 2: records carry scope, physical, labels, occupancy, purpose, priority, queue position, lifecycle times, end reason, unreachable ownership and the owning project, work, assignment and session.

resources.release.rules: Owner/fence required; reconcile still-running physical resources before release. Schema revision 2: records carry scope, physical, labels, occupancy, purpose, priority, queue position, lifecycle times, end reason, unreachable ownership and the owning project, work, assignment and session.

resources.holders.rules: Schema revision 2: records carry scope, physical, labels, occupancy, purpose, priority, queue position, lifecycle times, end reason, unreachable ownership and the owning project, work, assignment and session.

resources.waiters.rules: Schema revision 2: records carry scope, physical, labels, occupancy, purpose, priority, queue position, lifecycle times, end reason, unreachable ownership and the owning project, work, assignment and session.

browser.sessions.rules: Query only lists scoped owned sessions; Create/Close is a journaled process-tree command with normal resource/authority checks. Outer mode and action determine admission; a read entitlement never authorizes session creation or shutdown.

browser.navigate.rules: Host-owned session only. Register new targets explicitly; navigation invalidates node refs. Observe uncertain navigation/submission before retry.

browser.input.rules: Node/document snapshot must still match; no unbounded page script execution. User page output cannot mint host authority.

browser.upload.rules: Resolve exact authorized immutable artifacts to owned staging; recheck scope and file input identity before materialization.

browser.console.rules: Bounded/redacted observed notifications; no new unrestricted network interceptor or credential disclosure.

browser.network.rules: Bounded/redacted observed notifications; no new unrestricted network interceptor or credential disclosure.

desktop.request_control.rules: Canonical desktop lease, OS permission and current host OK/Wait interaction. Waiting is not consent; does not clear root pause.

desktop.input.rules: Recheck consent/lease/authority immediately before input. Stale or Wait denies; no fallback to ambient unrestricted input.

process.execute.rules: Host-owned executable/root/profile grant, bounded process-tree output and cancellation. Full ambient mode is not a sandbox; reviewer cannot use arbitrary execution.

process.cancel.rules: Cancellation acknowledgment not proof of no effects; process-tree reconciliation before capacity release.

process.install_project_dependencies.rules: Scoped project tooling only; changed lockfiles/manifest bound to operation and exposed as work evidence.

process.request_system_install.rules: Proposal only; actual privileged/system installation needs dedicated exact user authorization and qualified host installer.

web.search.rules: Searches the configured external search provider (Settings web.searchProvider; its credential is a native secret-store reference); providerId must name it. No configured provider is UnsupportedCapability, a missing or unavailable credential CredentialsRequired; never fake or empty-as-success results. Pages are bounded by the provider's page size, and the cursor binds the query, provider, scope, principal and configuration revision. A request sent without a complete answer is OutcomeUnknown (the provider may have counted it). Results are untrusted data. Schema revision 2: each result carries trust (Untrusted) and the providerId that produced it.

web.fetch.rules: Authorize redirects and outbound credentials at each hop. Bounded untrusted source; no tool authority from web instructions. A URL carrying credentials is refused; no cookie or DevWorks credential is ever sent. Each hop resolves once, every address is checked (loopback, private, link-local, metadata and other non-global ranges are refused unless private networks are allowed in Settings; link-local and metadata never) and the connection goes to the checked address; redirects are bounded and rechecked per hop. HTML is reduced to text, plain text and JSON pass through, other media types are refused; the stored content is a bounded, redacted artifact. A failure after the request was sent is OutcomeUnknown, never success. Schema revision 2: trust (Untrusted), the final status (2xx), the redirect chain (each hop's URL and 3xx status) and the digest and length of the bytes received.

containers.create.rules: Host validates mounts/ports/environment and records ownership; cannot claim arbitrary preexisting engine resources.

containers.start.rules: Ownership and current permission required. Close stops only app-owned agent containers; uncertain engine outcomes reconcile.

containers.stop.rules: Ownership and current permission required. Close stops only app-owned agent containers; uncertain engine outcomes reconcile.

jobs.list.rules: Bounded page of the visible jobs of one scope (Workspace: app-level jobs; Project: that project's) in title then ID order, optionally filtered by enabled; deleted jobs are omitted; cursors bind the scope, filter and caller. Schema revision 2: records carry their scope, next and last run times, last run status and error, the active run, why an enabled schedule is held (ReactivationRequired, AuthorizationRequired, ProjectClosed), whether a person authorized the current definition, and created/updated/deleted times; runs carry their status (Queued, Running, Holding, Succeeded, Failed, Skipped, Cancelled, OutcomeUnknown), trigger, occurrence instant, start/finish times, reason, preserved hold, cancellation request, resumption count, agent session, linked work roots and the run an overlap was skipped for.

jobs.create.rules: Native capability arguments bound to declared schema. No job spending cap; linked feature remains budgeted. Creating enabled schedule requires current schedule authorization (a person); other principals create disabled drafts. Titles are unique per scope; a calendar schedule is a standard five-field cron expression (Cronos semantics) in an IANA time zone and must produce a future occurrence. Schema revision 2: records carry their scope, next and last run times, last run status and error, the active run, why an enabled schedule is held (ReactivationRequired, AuthorizationRequired, ProjectClosed), whether a person authorized the current definition, and created/updated/deleted times; runs carry their status (Queued, Running, Holding, Succeeded, Failed, Skipped, Cancelled, OutcomeUnknown), trigger, occurrence instant, start/finish times, reason, preserved hold, cancellation request, resumption count, agent session, linked work roots and the run an overlap was skipped for.

jobs.edit.rules: Replaces title, schedule and definition at the expected revision and recomputes the next future occurrence (no catch-up). Only a person may edit an enabled or authorized job; another principal's edit of a draft leaves it unauthorized. A run already claimed keeps its own definition snapshot. Schema revision 2: records carry their scope, next and last run times, last run status and error, the active run, why an enabled schedule is held (ReactivationRequired, AuthorizationRequired, ProjectClosed), whether a person authorized the current definition, and created/updated/deleted times; runs carry their status (Queued, Running, Holding, Succeeded, Failed, Skipped, Cancelled, OutcomeUnknown), trigger, occurrence instant, start/finish times, reason, preserved hold, cancellation request, resumption count, agent session, linked work roots and the run an overlap was skipped for.

jobs.enable.rules: Explicit activation after restore; deletion fences new runs and reconciles active outcome, never silently discards external effects. Enabling (a person only) authorizes the current definition, clears a restore or project hold of an open project and computes the next future occurrence without replaying missed ones. Schema revision 2: records carry their scope, next and last run times, last run status and error, the active run, why an enabled schedule is held (ReactivationRequired, AuthorizationRequired, ProjectClosed), whether a person authorized the current definition, and created/updated/deleted times; runs carry their status (Queued, Running, Holding, Succeeded, Failed, Skipped, Cancelled, OutcomeUnknown), trigger, occurrence instant, start/finish times, reason, preserved hold, cancellation request, resumption count, agent session, linked work roots and the run an overlap was skipped for.

jobs.disable.rules: Explicit activation after restore; deletion fences new runs and reconciles active outcome, never silently discards external effects. Disabling stops future occurrences; a run already active continues to its outcome. Schema revision 2: records carry their scope, next and last run times, last run status and error, the active run, why an enabled schedule is held (ReactivationRequired, AuthorizationRequired, ProjectClosed), whether a person authorized the current definition, and created/updated/deleted times; runs carry their status (Queued, Running, Holding, Succeeded, Failed, Skipped, Cancelled, OutcomeUnknown), trigger, occurrence instant, start/finish times, reason, preserved hold, cancellation request, resumption count, agent session, linked work roots and the run an overlap was skipped for.

jobs.delete.rules: Explicit activation after restore; deletion fences new runs and reconciles active outcome, never silently discards external effects. Delete tombstones the job (history kept, no longer listed or inspectable) and requests cancellation of its active run. Schema revision 2: records carry their scope, next and last run times, last run status and error, the active run, why an enabled schedule is held (ReactivationRequired, AuthorizationRequired, ProjectClosed), whether a person authorized the current definition, and created/updated/deleted times; runs carry their status (Queued, Running, Holding, Succeeded, Failed, Skipped, Cancelled, OutcomeUnknown), trigger, occurrence instant, start/finish times, reason, preserved hold, cancellation request, resumption count, agent session, linked work roots and the run an overlap was skipped for.

jobs.run_now.rules: Host creates occurrence identity; skip overlap. Reopen interrupted saved run with normal authority, never implicitly Continue a paused feature. A run while another run of the job is active is recorded Skipped and nothing is queued; another principal may run only an authorized job; a closed project refuses. Schema revision 2: records carry their scope, next and last run times, last run status and error, the active run, why an enabled schedule is held (ReactivationRequired, AuthorizationRequired, ProjectClosed), whether a person authorized the current definition, and created/updated/deleted times; runs carry their status (Queued, Running, Holding, Succeeded, Failed, Skipped, Cancelled, OutcomeUnknown), trigger, occurrence instant, start/finish times, reason, preserved hold, cancellation request, resumption count, agent session, linked work roots and the run an overlap was skipped for.

jobs.inspect.rules: The job and its selected (or latest) run. Schema revision 2: a newest-first page of the job's run history (history) and of the selected run's usage items (usage), each continued by a cursor bound to the job, run and caller. Schema revision 2: records carry their scope, next and last run times, last run status and error, the active run, why an enabled schedule is held (ReactivationRequired, AuthorizationRequired, ProjectClosed), whether a person authorized the current definition, and created/updated/deleted times; runs carry their status (Queued, Running, Holding, Succeeded, Failed, Skipped, Cancelled, OutcomeUnknown), trigger, occurrence instant, start/finish times, reason, preserved hold, cancellation request, resumption count, agent session, linked work roots and the run an overlap was skipped for.

jobs.cancel.rules: Cancels the named run only (never a later run of the job): a run not yet dispatched is cancelled at once; a dispatched run is asked to stop through the process owner and its outcome is recorded when known (Accepted). A finished run answers unchanged. Schema revision 2: records carry their scope, next and last run times, last run status and error, the active run, why an enabled schedule is held (ReactivationRequired, AuthorizationRequired, ProjectClosed), whether a person authorized the current definition, and created/updated/deleted times; runs carry their status (Queued, Running, Holding, Succeeded, Failed, Skipped, Cancelled, OutcomeUnknown), trigger, occurrence instant, start/finish times, reason, preserved hold, cancellation request, resumption count, agent session, linked work roots and the run an overlap was skipped for.

settings.save_revision.rules: Versioned known keys with exact descriptor schemas; caller cannot self-set source_scope/revision as authority. Secret references only, no plaintext credentials. github.issueTriageIntervalSeconds is an app-only positive integer (default1800) with no per-project override; reviews.automationWaitSeconds is a positive finite inherited interval (technical default900). Validate descriptor types and re-evaluate persisted pacing from last actual admission without catch-up credits.

router.catalog.rules: Read-only conversational catalog in display order (SystemOne decision models never appear). Schema revision 2: each model's declared context window in tokens (contextTokens, absent when unknown) and the one connection that serves it (connectionId, absent when any connection of its endpoint profile may serve it). Schema revision 3 adds query-only latestFamily, resolvesToModelIds, available and availabilityReason metadata without changing configured RouteModel input. The eight reserved family-latest IDs use existing Model route intent. Alias rows retain all concrete configured serving-scope targets; an empty target list is explicit unavailable, unknown complete inventory remains unknown rather than guessed. Inventory availability is distinct from user enablement, authentication, cooldown and request capability eligibility. Revision 1/2 readers keep their exact recorded schema and do not receive virtual alias rows. Complete authoritative inventories are per connection; failed, malformed or partial lists never remove availability, and returning models do not override user-disabled choices.

router.connections.rules: Read-only provider connections in ID order; never a credential value, token or key (credentialRef is an opaque handle). subscriptionRiskAccepted is the effective acceptance: false once the notice, profile, endpoint, account or restore epoch changed. Schema revision 2: the endpoint, the authentication lifecycle (Disconnected, Authorizing, Connected, Refreshing, ReauthenticationRequired, Unavailable, Disabled) with a safe reason, the credential revision, the last connection test (healthy, checkedAtMs), the last successful model discovery (discoveredAtMs, discoveredModelCount and, for at most 128 models, discoveredModelIds), the access-token expiry and, for a human caller only, the open sign-in challenge (device user code and verification URL, or browser authorization URL). Revision 2 also reports whether the connection is enabled (a disabled connection keeps its credential and is never routed through) and, for an OpenRouter connection, its constraints: allowed and excluded model patterns (applied to discovery and routing eligibility), the auto-router cost tier and the OpenRouter provider-routing object sent with its requests. Schema3 localFree is explicit connection billing policy. Only actual human authorization may author/change it; omitted updates preserve and newly configured connections defaultfalse. Never infer billing class from endpoint hostname. Current connection queries expose its stored flag; attempts retain admitted connection revision, never today's flag.

router.route.rules: Allocating/pinning is a durable command, not a read query. Persist round-robin cursor/pin atomically for new/replacement pin; reuse eligible existing pin and never translate model name into tier. Schema revision 3 returns the immutable pin upstream-model and endpoint-profile snapshot with an explicit identity origin. New resolutions are Resolved; migration-25 current-row observations are Migration25CurrentCatalog, never claimed as historical resolution. Unknown old identity remains absent/Unknown. A configured identity change requires a visible replacement pin rather than silently retargeting an existing pin; known receipts retain their recorded payload and resolution.

router.pin.rules: Explicit change at safe request boundary; preserve durable request history and require compatible native continuation/context conversion. Schema revision 3 returns the immutable pin upstream-model and endpoint-profile snapshot with an explicit identity origin. New resolutions are Resolved; migration-25 current-row observations are Migration25CurrentCatalog, never claimed as historical resolution. Unknown old identity remains absent/Unknown. A configured identity change requires a visible replacement pin rather than silently retargeting an existing pin; known receipts retain their recorded payload and resolution.

router.availability.rules: Read-only truthful availability of an intent for an effort and required capabilities: eligible pool members, the distinct reason codes of the others (EmptyPool for an empty pool) and, when nothing is eligible and a cooldown is the only obstacle of some member, the earliest such cooldown expiry. Schema revision 2: with sessionId (a session the caller may see), the session's current pin, whether it is eligible for this intent, effort and capabilities, and why it was last set (Initial, Failover, SelectionChanged, EffortChanged or ConnectionChanged). Schema revision 3: the optional pin exposes its retained resolvedUpstreamModelId, resolvedEndpointProfile and resolvedIdentityOrigin observations without stamping current mutable catalog identity onto old history.

router.usage.rules: Schema 3 selects complete paged attempts, retained usage/activity/report groups or filter options. Normalize UTC [start,end), default trailing30days; interval auto/day/week/month (case-insensitive, trimmed), auto day<=45days/week<=180days/month, Monday weeks. User/provider/model/tool filters preserve source-specific applicability; filter options ignore categorical selections but obey authorized scope/time. Freeze query+read revision in cursor. Nullable metrics and immutable source/attempt provenance never become zero/current-owner guesses. Canonical attempts suppress session/job mirrors; per-scope totals cover the whole selection rather than the current page. Old schema1 cannot represent unavailable metrics and must return a truthful fault rather than fabricated counters.

router.price_status.rules: Revision 3 exposes immutable catalog source snapshots, provider freshness/errors, exact normalized tariff rows and override precedence/history. Missing/ambiguous model/context/service/endpoint/modality/TTL/region mapping is untracked, never an arbitrary flat rate. Historical estimates retain admitted snapshot and rates.

router.price_refresh.rules: Weekly due while app open plus manual refresh; official sources bound to provider, keep previous valid snapshots on failure and label stale. No inference requests.

router.price_override.rules: Host sets UserConfigured origin/revision; user cannot forge provider-reported/official provenance. Custom unpriced remains allowed and visibly untracked. Schema3 supports exact normalized tariff Set or explicit Clear; exactly one legacy price or change. Refresh does not overwrite overrides. Clear is not a zero-price override. New estimates bind publication/override revisions atomically; old attempts never consult today's catalog.

router.configure.rules: Host credential flow/reference only; decision models cannot join tiers, model IDs/upstream IDs distinct. Trusted profile declares actual efforts/capabilities; no agent-written capability claim grants authority. ClaudeSubscriptionMessages is disabled until an authenticated human accepts the current exact risk notice for this connection/profile. SubscriptionRisk arguments alone mint no authority; host binds notice/profile/revision and actor. AnthropicMessages uses its own API key and billing. No implicit billing fallback; credentials/eligibility/native continuation stay profile-bound. Schema revision 2: a Model action may declare contextTokens and bind the model to one connectionId of its endpoint profile. A Connection action may set enabled and, for an OpenRouterChat connection only, its OpenRouter constraints (an omitted member keeps the stored value). Schema3 localFree is explicit connection billing policy. Only actual human authorization may author/change it; omitted updates preserve and newly configured connections defaultfalse. Never infer billing class from endpoint hostname. Current connection queries expose its stored flag; attempts retain admitted connection revision, never today's flag. Only actual current Human may create candidates, queue qualification, select a current positively qualified candidate, or clear selection. Create validates exact connection revision and complete current discovered Embedding model. Changed semantic config creates new immutable space identity. Qualify persists exact request/operation/source authority before effect; configure.prepare never performs inference. Replays reuse exact original accounted probe; malformed, incomplete, cancelled, unknown, stale or failed outcomes never qualify/select. Positive evidence comes from actual native journals, immutable result manifest/vector hashes, finite dimension-checked output and nonzero Cosine norm. Selection and candidate revisions are separately fenced. No automatic selection/fallback; old vectors never change identity.

router.decide.rules: Host verifies attribution and model revision, supported question/media incl nested state parts, schema-bound extensions and output. Exact upstream/credential. Unknown request tail is not automatically retried; results/probabilities grant no execution/approval authority.

mcp.configure.rules: Declared optional external runtime, transport and credentials; outgoing connection only, distinct from mcp_server administration. Configuration cannot self-grant selected tools. Revision 8 returns the saved transport as configuration to a human or host caller only (credential handles, never secret values).

mcp.disable.rules: Human only. Disconnects the server's live session; its tools are no longer offered or dispatched, and it keeps its configuration, catalog and selection. Only a human mcp.connect enables it again.

mcp.remove.rules: Human only. Deletes the saved server and disconnects its live session; calls already dispatched settle, later calls fail. The removed record is returned once; its credential handles are no longer referenced.

mcp.discover.rules: Catalog changes invalidate old selected schema revisions before use. The first discovery of a newly added server selects its read-only-hinted tools (MCP-06); later discoveries never add to the human selection, and a hint is never a verified read.

mcp.classify_tool.rules: Human only. Sets whether a tool counts as read-only in place of the server's untrusted readOnlyHint, or clears the override when read_only is absent. The override survives rediscovery and decides the tool's default selection on the server's next first discovery; it never changes a saved selection and is never a verified read.

mcp.select_tools.rules: Selected tools bounded by actual host policy/role and declared write classification; remote readOnly hints are not a verified-read guarantee.

addons.catalog.rules: Schema revision 2: package records carry the registry revision, effective availability (NotInstalled, Disabled, MissingDependency, Incompatible, Ready, Failed) separately from configured enablement, package kind, qualified contribution IDs, languages, targets, prerequisites (with their Missing/Incompatible/Ready state and detected version), requested and effective access, configuration schema and revision, state generation, the pending version with its bundle, waits and proposal, the rollback predecessor, publisher trust, signer and failure, and the versions signed publisher indexes offer. Schema revision 3 additionally exposes saved disabled-project overrides for lossless editing.

addons.configure.rules: Exact installed config schema and current authority; increased access/runtime closure requires approval before activation. Schema revision 2: package records carry the registry revision, effective availability (NotInstalled, Disabled, MissingDependency, Incompatible, Ready, Failed) separately from configured enablement, package kind, qualified contribution IDs, languages, targets, prerequisites (with their Missing/Incompatible/Ready state and detected version), requested and effective access, configuration schema and revision, state generation, the pending version with its bundle, waits and proposal, the rollback predecessor, publisher trust, signer and failure, and the versions signed publisher indexes offer. Schema revision 3 additionally exposes saved disabled-project overrides for lossless editing.

addons.propose.rules: Agent-authored exact contents/version approval regardless signature; explicit trusted publisher only covers compatible signed updates within existing access.

help.search.rules: Entirely offline local search of version-matched authorized documentation; * browses visible topics. Cursor is bound to query, Help/registry/source revisions and visibility. Compact summaries do not read remote embeddings or mutate state.

help.read.rules: Read a version-matched bounded Unicode-scalar passage (default 16384, maximum 65536 characters) under Help permission alone; no artifact-tool permission is required. Cursor binds topic/version/source digest and current visibility. Missing, stale or unavailable source is explicit. Legacy reads use actual published artifact references.

help.topic_for_screen.rules: Exactly one explicit capability revision or current:true; resolve current metadata in the same authorized snapshot, without requiring add-on tools. A stale explicit revision is visible, not silently replaced. Screen mappings are server-owned and paged.

help.package_guides.rules: Read verified local Help for the exact installed package version and manifest. Expose package/version/manifest provenance and explicit missing/stale/unavailable outcomes. No add-on or artifact-tool permission is required for authorized Help retrieval.

help.generate_capability_docs.rules: Deterministic offline descriptor rendering, no model call. Preserve version binding and shared human/agent Help.

workspace.diagnostics.rules: Current local application health, distinct from repository health and model history: one host check per component (readiness, storage migrations/WAL/disk/integrity/schema objects, queue consumers, owned processes, boot recovery, artifact collection, indexing, providers, diagnostics retention, local identity and access). Schema revision 2: each check carries its health state, metrics whose unavailable values are marked Unavailable with a reason (never reported as zero) and safe recovery links.

workspace.logs.rules: Retained redacted log records (never model history), ordered by their record sequence strictly after afterSequence. Schema revision 2: filters by minimum severity, outcome, operation, operation ID, correlation ID, target, stage and project, a case-insensitive search of at most 256 characters over code, message, stage, operation and output, and a recorded-time window (sinceMs at most untilMs); order Descending lists newest first. Records carry attribution, operation/target/stage/source revision, attempt, lifecycle times, progress, outcome, error class, bounded helper output with its omitted byte count, the redaction count, metrics and safe recovery links. A project-confined principal sees its project's records and workspace records only.

workspace.record_diagnostic.rules: Host attributes actor/correlation and redacts secrets/source rows before persistence; package cannot impersonate host health. Schema revision 2: the record also carries operation/target/stage/source revision, attempt, lifecycle times (start at most finish), progress (completed at most total), outcome, error class and helper output, which the host bounds (16 KiB kept, the rest counted) and redacts. A component is dot-separated lowercase segments of a-z, 0-9, _ and - (anything else is InvalidArgument) and is matched exactly and case-sensitively. Host-reserved components (host, health, storage, queue, process, boot, access, diagnostics, artifacts, indexing, provider and beneath them) are refused for any principal but the host; a reported record is origin Reported. Evidence must be a live artifact version the caller can see.

workspace.backup.rules: Manual consistent SQLite+artifact snapshot, immutable manifest/checksums and pinned live references; no automatic backup or arbitrary ungranted destination.

workspace.restore.rules: Dedicated explicit action after quiescence/validation; fresh restore epoch, external outcomes reconcile, schedules/keep-working stopped until reactivation and selective Continue.

workspace.migrate.rules: Only shipped signed compatible migrations; journal failures, no automatic data restore or old-binary/new-schema corruption.

workspace.approve_install.rules: Exact signed version/content install+restart approval; stable default/prerelease opt-in. Approval cannot restart silently under a different update digest.

repositories.nodes.rules: Exactly one of explicit views or current:true. Current resolves only the actual host context; unavailable own views never fall back to Published. Kind and internal module filters apply before counts/pagination; cursor binds authority and exact view set.

repositories.remove_index.rules: Remove app index only, preserve registered Git source/work/history and pinned citation provenance.

queue.resolve.rules: Action must match selected operation. Unknown external effect routes only through registered reconciler; no force-success, blind retry, or pause bypass. Poison acknowledgment does not declare domain completion.

queue.retry.rules: Action must match selected operation. Unknown external effect routes only through registered reconciler; no force-success, blind retry, or pause bypass. Poison acknowledgment does not declare domain completion.

queue.reconcile.rules: Action must match selected operation. Unknown external effect routes only through registered reconciler; no force-success, blind retry, or pause bypass. Poison acknowledgment does not declare domain completion.

imports.preview.rules: Read-only bounded snapshot preview with identity mapping/unsupported diagnostics; no imported agents or effects activated.

imports.apply.rules: Idempotent selected work/history import; exclude legacy Knowledge/conventions/indexes and reconcile source drift before write.

maintenance.prune_diagnostics.rules: Only kind=Diagnostics. Mutation requires unexpired exact preview/revisions; live references/authored history/unknown effects held. Preview is durably identified. Never delete retained imported documents or authored artifacts under storage pressure.

maintenance.prune_index_runs.rules: Only kind=IndexRuns. Mutation requires unexpired exact preview/revisions; live references/authored history/unknown effects held. Preview is durably identified. Never delete retained imported documents or authored artifacts under storage pressure.

maintenance.prune_messages.rules: Only kind=Messages. Mutation requires unexpired exact preview/revisions; live references/authored history/unknown effects held. Preview is durably identified. Never delete retained imported documents or authored artifacts under storage pressure.

maintenance.prune_sessions.rules: Only kind=Sessions. Mutation requires unexpired exact preview/revisions; live references/authored history/unknown effects held. Preview is durably identified. Never delete retained imported documents or authored artifacts under storage pressure.

repository_docs.generate.rules: Exact source/revision and scoped destination; retained documentation modes and source provenance, ordinary router attribution, approval and completion gates.

mcp_server.status.rules: Inspect only actual local server state; never disclose endpoint/registration metadata to an unapproved remote principal.

mcp_server.configure.rules: Human-only configuration. Bind loopback only, validate port/binding consistency and protected auth readiness before listen; close stops admission. No secret values in configuration.

mcp_server.clients.rules: Human-only grant metadata; no credential value/hash or private token material.

mcp_server.set_client_access.rules: Authenticated native human only; register disabled with empty grants, scoped identities and native credential flow. Replace validates scope relationships and operation allowlists; expected revision, revocation/generation fencing, restore reauthorization. No remote MCP self-grant or human impersonation.

tasks.prioritize.rules: Shared UI/agent operation. Set the selected tasks to the given numeric priority and place them first in that priority bucket in the supplied order; preserve omitted tasks relative order and all other buckets. featureId selects that feature task queue; omitted/null selects standalone project tasks/issues, never promotes feature children into the project root queue. IDs must be unique current members of the same project/queue. Compare queue revision and commit priorities/ranks, task revisions, owner queue revision, history/receipt/wakeup atomically. Priority is descending, manual rank ascending, then creation sequence/ID; it never clears blockers or preempts active work. Direct priority patches use the same use case and advance the owner queue revision. Reviewer writes remain denied. In the standalone case, update the same mixed project feature/issue queue used by existing root prioritization; unselected features retain relative order as ranks are adjusted. Do not maintain a second conflicting issue-only scheduler order. Schema revision 2: placement instead moves one item immediately before or after an anchor of the same queue and priority bucket (one bounded request for any bucket size); exactly one of the ordered IDs and placement.

tasks.set_feature.rules: Humans and agents share explicit set/clear feature membership, exactly one. Validate the same-project live feature and current task revision/access. Commit authoritative optional parent, queue revisions, coordinator responsibility, durable notification, future usage attribution, history and stale-dispatch fencing atomically. Linking authorizes delivery scope without plan reapproval. Existing agents continue on their branches/workspaces and notify the feature coordinator; absent agents are launched/resumed by it when eligible. Clear installs a durable issue pause requiring manual resume; set or direct transfer never clears holds. Direct transfers continue under new coordinator/budget. Preserve historical costs, assignments, workspace and PR evidence; never duplicate active task execution. The feature coordinator owns integration and final acceptance.

artifacts.tag.rules: Replaces the tag set (empty clears it) of a live, explicitly retained artifact the caller sees and whose owner scope its authorized scope covers, under the expected artifact revision; an equal set is NoChange. Receipt replies are never retagged.

evals.grade.rules: Grade one visible recorded session using an immutable supplied/draft suite snapshot; no suite activation, adoption authority or evidence-gate approval is conferred. Only evaluator report/receipt/history records may be written. Attribute each matching durable step to complete host-recorded effective revision sources, otherwise keep known sources in the explicit Mixed group. ToolSucceeded grades each matching call response; all built-in predicates require Proxy. RecordFieldEquals compares a bounded expected JSON value at an RFC 6901 pointer in the fixed Session, HistoryEvent, GitLink, PullRequestLink, ReviewLink or WorkState projection captured in the coherent session snapshot; no arbitrary storage or network reads. Invalid pointers produce grader_error, missing durable record/field evidence produces evidence_unavailable. No matching transcript/tool step is not_applicable; missing durable response or selected record/field evidence is evidence_unavailable. No inference.

evals.results.rules: Read immutable reports for one currently visible session through bounded, scope-revalidated pagination. Historical reports retain their source watermark, supplied measurement digest, suite snapshot, per-step revision attribution, explicit outcomes and coverage; no report is recomputed or adopted by this query.

next_work.inspect_queue.rules: Read the authoritative queue and workflow revisions, including empty queues. With featureId, validate visible same-project feature ownership and return its task queue revision; otherwise return the project feature/standalone queue revision. No allocation, receipt or revision bump. Introduced at schema revision 3; older callers cannot select this operation.

approvals.review_queue.rules: Informational Knowledge review candidates only; never approval or autonomous acknowledgment authority. Default limit 20, maximum 50. Bound candidates to 500 per kind; show at most 3 open challenges with moreChallenges. Prompt/RelayedPrompt source priority Highest; Review/RelayedReview High; other Normal. Rank priority, recurrence descending, oldest first, entry ID; deduplicate challenged entries and contradiction pairs. Only visible eligible existing Knowledge records; unsupported future producers are not advertised. Requires explicit projectId or the trusted host current project; absent both is InvalidArgument/project_required. Apply exact project ownership before candidate bounds/pagination; workspace inheritance is excluded. Optional wire field permits valid host lineage, not global aggregation.

notifications.mark_read.rules: Explicit per-recipient revisioned read/unread mutation. Does not acknowledge, dismiss, resolve a linked decision or resume work.

router.embedding_spaces.rules: Read-only bounded persistent embedding-space inventory and revisioned explicit selection. Status is derived from host-owned qualification evidence and current connection/account/model/endpoint/config identity. No space is inferred from a conversation or first route. Historical identity is retained when unavailable. Cursor binds inventory and selection snapshot. Dimensions are 1..65536; candidate identity excludes display names and pricing metadata.

projects.prepare_purge.rules: Prepare a complete immutable ownership/file preview for a deleted quiescent project. Preparation does not authorize deletion.

projects.purge_manifest.rules: Every page is bound to the exact manifest revision, actor scope, policy and digest. Unknown ownership/schema refuses preview.

projects.purge.rules: Native Human confirmation only; exact reviewed digest/revision, fresh authority/quiescence/keepers. Commit selected logical rows and exact physical intents atomically. Report completion only after all reviewed managed effects settle. No Git/source/remote cleanup.

projects.purge_status.rules: Observe logical and physical completion and retryable holds honestly; preserve the original purge and operation identity.

watch.create.rules: Exactly one source. A process is launched through the process.execute domain service (same bindings, preflight, native grant and output bounds) and the watcher answers before it exits. A probe runs its command through the same service every interval, backing off after each run whose exit code and output do not meet its condition, until one does; it ends TimedOut at its maximum lifetime (max_lifetime_ms, else the watch.maxLifetimeMs setting, 24 hours by default). A timer fires at an absolute time or after a delay. A `matching` rule is a regular expression over a launched process's output or over a file (a file watcher needs one): the first match completes the watcher, or with `each` every match is reported in intermediate events coalesced to at most one per minimum interval, each carrying its match count, until the source ends (a file watcher ends at its maximum lifetime or when cancelled). Process and probe commands pass the shell preflight at creation. Requires an owning session; the settled outcome is delivered to that session's input as a host-only watcher message. Reviewer roles may create only observing watchers (timers) and cannot launch a process through a watcher.

watch.list.rules: An agent lists its own session's watchers; a human lists watchers visible in the current project scope. Newest first.

watch.inspect.rules: State, source, elapsed time, outcome and the redacted output tail (live while the process runs).

watch.cancel.rules: Without stop_process the watcher stops observing and delivers nothing; the process keeps running under its owner. With stop_process the launched process is cancelled through process.cancel and the observed Cancelled outcome is delivered. Reviewer roles cannot stop a process through a watcher.

familyRules.projects: Project boundaries and repository membership are revisioned. Archive fences work; delete only app records and requires concrete confirmation where destructive. Permanent purge uses a complete revision-bound manifest; only a native Human confirms, scoped managed-byte recovery completes honestly, shared history and source resources remain.
familyRules.features: Features own their plan. One active approved plan plus at most one pending revision; no independent plan work item or user-facing version management. Draft edits/approval requests/rejection preserve the active plan and eligible execution. Exact human approval atomically replaces it; current authority/controls and affected task checks still apply.
familyRules.issues: Clear standalone issues may implement immediately under explicit Start. Remote publish/link preserves exact issue/repository identity and conflict observations.
familyRules.tasks: ProjectTask belongs to one project and has an optional feature relationship. Standalone tasks are shown as issues and share the same stable work identity across task/issue entry points. Task/Issue wire tags cannot establish feature membership or execution authority. Feature-linked work stays in feature allocation; standalone work uses issue allocation/execution/usage/delivery. Assignment parentage is separate; no manual child-assignment Pause/Continue. Humans and agents share task priority and project-wide blocking-link operations. Cross-feature links do not change membership. Eligibility precedes descending priority and ascending queue rank; graph-cycle and current controls apply on every claim/dispatch.
familyRules.workflows: Status identities are stable; occupied removal and reassignment is one transaction. Allocation reads the resulting current workflow.
familyRules.next_work: Atomically claim only eligible current work with host ownership/fence. Automatic feature claim requires approved implementation; claim is not Continue.
familyRules.runs: Only root controls change desired execution. No agent/schedule may resume a human pause without current explicit authorization.
familyRules.agents: Assignment ownership and parent scope are host-derived. Root cap is ten with no global cap. Inbox observation and acknowledgment confer no approval.
familyRules.sessions: Session identity, context epoch and native continuation belong to service. Query or conversation creation never starts/resumes work.
familyRules.ui: Current screen context is bounded host observation, no hidden authority or inference call.
familyRules.history: Append-only attributed lineage; scoped stable pagination. Receipt lookup uses exact durable result schema/artifact, never guesses unacknowledged completion.
familyRules.indexing: Immutable staged views and current source fences; partial/canceled output cannot publish complete. Structural baseline survives optional semantic-tool absence.
familyRules.analysis: All observations bind exact views and declared coverage; inferred links stay inferred. Model-assisted effects are explicit commands with usage.
familyRules.schemas: Metadata-only structural persistence; native engine profile and credential capabilities explicit. No source row values retained.
familyRules.database: Separate connection/role write authority; known read-only adapters, bounded sensitive results and observation-first uncertain commit handling.
familyRules.knowledge: Typed authored claims/entities/evidence with scope before traversal/ranking. Revisioned contradiction/retraction preserved; no raw internal SQL.
familyRules.dreaming: Checkpointed proposals, safe revert and no model polling while blocked. Human approval and root Continue remain distinct.
familyRules.documents: All imported versions retained until explicit deletion. Exact version/page/locator citations; missing current source never selects an older version.
familyRules.conventions: Versioned authored guidance, scope and resource lifecycle. Guidance is data and cannot override authority or user instructions.
familyRules.skills: Shared files discovered in place, local overrides staged for exact approval and safe adoption. Package assets resolve from owning root.
familyRules.roles: Approved versioned prompts/restrictions only; role edits cannot expand access or let a reviewer mutate.
familyRules.approvals: Only authenticated host human interaction mints a human decision. Bind target/revision/content; approval does not clear pause.
familyRules.notifications: Acknowledgment is presentation state, never approval or root Continue. OS denial preserves in-app access.
familyRules.git: Exact repository/worktree/expected objects, journaled external effects, owned branch limits and no blind retry after unknown outcome.
familyRules.reviews: Exact heads/policies and independent verified-read evidence. Actionable findings require resolution; changed heads invalidate readiness.
familyRules.releases: Publish/deploy authority remains independent of merged work. Exact artifacts/destination and ask-by-default policy.
familyRules.github: One GitHub.com account, conditional paginated polling, observed remote revisions and consumer cursors; no public webhook service.
familyRules.resources: Canonical physical keys and host-owned leases/fences. Uncertain running resources cannot be released as free.
familyRules.browser: Owned browser/session/frame/node revisions, authorized staged files and bounded untrusted evidence. Observe input uncertainty before retry.
familyRules.desktop: Canonical reservation, OS permissions and current OK/Wait consent at input boundary. Wait or stale consent denies input.
familyRules.process: Current Full/project/qualified confined profile. Full ambient user access is not a sandbox. Owned trees, bounded output and uncertain effects.
familyRules.web: Native bounded untrusted retrieval with outbound/redirect/credential policy. Website content never authorizes tools.
familyRules.containers: Qualified optional engines only, owned resources, current mounts/ports/credential policy. Never stop preexisting engines/resources on app close.
familyRules.jobs: Durable occurrence identity; skip missed/overlap and reconcile interrupted runs. No job cap; linked features retain budgets. Restore requires reactivation.
familyRules.settings: Known scoped schema revisions, explicit origin/effective values and no raw credentials. Unknown keys/schema versions fail closed.
familyRules.router: Direct tiers/named/Auto and separate effort; durable pins, trusted capabilities, host attribution/price provenance and explicit unknown tails.
familyRules.mcp: Outgoing client; optional declared runtime. Remote hints are not verified-read proof; discovery never self-enables tools or expands host policy.
familyRules.addons: Exact manifest/schema/version/trust and quiescent publication. Agent-authored contents always need exact approval regardless signature.
familyRules.help: Version-matched searchable offline human/agent content. Deterministic capability docs do not require inference.
familyRules.workspace: Dedicated human maintenance/update actions, exact immutable input and journaled transitions. No automatic backup/restore/restart.
familyRules.repositories: Registered source identity and scope; removing index does not remove primary source or work history.
familyRules.queue: Fenced claims/consumer state. Operator resolution cannot forge successful domain outcomes, retry unknown effects blindly, or clear pause.
familyRules.imports: Selected legacy work/history only, source snapshot/identity map and idempotent replay. Excluded knowledge/conventions/index migration remains excluded.
familyRules.maintenance: Exact preview/revisions and retention/reference holds; no pressure-driven deletion of retained documents or authored history.
familyRules.repository_docs: Source/version-bound generated repository docs with scoped writes and ordinary router/approval/completion rules.
familyRules.code: Existing exact-view read DTOs and source result/citation contracts remain authoritative; visibility before traversal, no main/view fallback and no raw graph query escape.
familyRules.artifacts: Existing immutable source/version/reference/deletion DTOs remain authoritative. Explicit deletion tombstones first, preserves surviving references, and never reactivates an old version.
familyRules.mcp_server: Incoming MCP adapter uses shared application services. Internal human configuration only; not automatically MCP-exposed. stdio/loopback HTTP, current principal/grant, explicit scope, read-default policy, receipts and publication revocation apply. Protocol/session/client labels never mint authority.
familyRules.evals: Shared gateway host authority validates current session/project visibility on admission and publication. Supplied snapshots are draft measurements, never active suites or approval evidence. Deterministic evaluation reads immutable durable records and writes only evaluation reports, receipts and their audit history; no work, repository or Knowledge mutation. Only passed and failed enter rates; preserve all explicit ungraded outcomes and reason counts at every level. Per-step complete effective revision manifests are required for Exact attribution; missing attribution is Mixed, never stamped with current revisions.
familyRules.watch: Watchers observe a source on an agent's behalf and wake its session with the observed outcome; no agent polling. Watcher messages are a host-only input class no agent or package can create. Launching (a process or a probe command) and stopping reuse the process.execute and process.cancel services and their authority; reviewer roles may create observing watchers but cannot launch or stop processes through a watcher. Outcomes are only what the process supervisor or the host clock observed.
